Bio of Dr. Maryna Kuzmenko

I created this page to make life easier for dear event organisers, journalists, podcast hosts, collaborators, and conference teams — a practical resource for anyone who needs a clear, accurate, publication-ready bio of Dr. Maryna Kuzmenko.

Professional bio

Dr. Maryna Kuzmenko brings nearly 10 years of practical experience in applying digital technologies in agriculture, with a primary focus on computer vision and deep learning for plant phenotyping and food quality assurance.

She is co-founder and CEO of Petiole, a UK-based SME developing practical AI tools for agriculture and plant science. The global platform Petiole Pro, developed by Maryna’s team, was named a finalist in the GIST Tech-I 2015 competition in the USA, shortlisted for the UK FPC Fresh Awards 2023, and received three grants from Innovate UK — the UK government’s innovation agency — and one Horizon Europe grant, for practical AI applications in agricultural challenges such as pest and disease detection.

Maryna was recognised as an Expert Top Voice on LinkedIn in the May 2026 edition and has an active educational presence in social and business media.

Dr Maryna Kuzmenko is a winner of the Innovate UK Women in Innovation Award 2025/26, announced on 5 August 2026, for MooMore — an AI and thermal imaging system that detects inflammation in dairy cows before lameness develops. The award carries a £75,000 grant and a twelve-month programme running to June 2027. She was one of 61 grant winners among 100 women founders recognised from 1,590 applications. Innovate UK project page · Why I moved from crops to cattle

She is one of 16 Community Forum Members of the 2025/26 Cohort, pre-selected by the Innovate UK Women in Innovation team. Maryna is also an Oxford Farming Conference 2026 Inspire Fellow.

Maryna is a fellow of the “Scaling Young Women’s Businesses Through IP Mentorship” programme by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) and the International Trade Centre’s SheTrades initiative. She is Virgin StartUp Alumna 2020.

She is a regular speaker at educational events and has participated in high-level agriculture-focused meetings in the United Kingdom and internationally.

Short bio — 300 characters

Dr Maryna Kuzmenko is a UK agritech founder applying AI to agriculture. She founded MooMore, using thermal imaging to detect dairy lameness before it shows, and won the Innovate UK Women in Innovation Award 2026. She previously built Petiole Pro's crop analysis tools.

100-word bio

Dr Maryna Kuzmenko is a UK-based agritech founder applying AI to agricultural productivity. She founded MooMore, which uses thermal imaging and on-device AI to detect inflammation in dairy cows days before lameness becomes visible, and won the Innovate UK Women in Innovation Award 2026 for it. The problem is the one she has always worked on: a measurement that matters is locked behind specialist equipment, so the people who need it never take it. With Petiole Pro that measurement was leaf area and the answer was a smartphone camera — tools now used by research organisations on six continents. She teaches AI in agriculture to more than 3,000 students across 119 countries.

Speaker introduction

First-person bio

I founded MooMore to catch lameness in dairy cows before anyone can see it. Thermal imaging and on-device AI pick up the inflammation days before the limp, and we're validating it now on a 650-cow herd in Staffordshire. In 2026 it won the Innovate UK Women in Innovation Award. Before this I spent a decade on the crop side, building measurement tools now used by research organisations on six continents.
